description: Work out the change-order amount from a material escalation clause using a base and current price index, a threshold and a cap. Use this tested BusCalc worksheet when the task matches its inputs and scope. Returns named results, units, formula, assumptions, method version, reference-value notes (official figure or your figure, with source and effective date), a check link and a source-page URL. Official reference values are prefilled when omitted; supply every other figure from the user's records. Percent fields take percent numbers. No figures are looked up; no private projects or purchases are accessed. Put tool fields inside inputs. Put tool fields inside inputs. Supply units or modelVersion only when listed in inputSchema. Follow its required fields and exact choices. Do not pass the REST calculator field inside MCP arguments.

baseAmount.description: Base contract material amount (US dollars). The material cost in the contract that the escalation clause covers.

baseIndex.description: Base index value. The index value for the base month named in the contract, such as a BLS Producer Price Index.

cap.description: Cap on the adjustment (0 = no cap). Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. The most the price can move, as a percent of the base material amount.

currentIndex.description: Current index value. The index value for the adjustment month, from the same index series.

mode.description: How the threshold works. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for how the threshold works. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: deductible = Deductible: only the change beyond the threshold is adjusted; trigger = Trigger: once passed, the whole change is adjusted.

threshold.description: Threshold before any adjustment. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. The index change the clause ignores, as a percent of the base index. Enter 0 if none.

twoWay.description: Do decreases lower the price too?. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for do decreases lower the price too?. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: yes = Yes, adjust up and down; no = No, increases only.

modelVersion.description: Optional expected method version; a mismatch is rejected.

name: buscalc_material_price_escalation_clause_adjustment

checkURL.description: Link that replays this calculation on https://buscalc.com/sumtru/verify/. Null when the inputs hold free-form text or the link would be too long.

notes.description: Reference-value notes first, then model notes and the standard limit statement.

referenceValues.description: One entry per official reference value in play: the official figure, the figure used, status official or user, source, effective date and the note text.

sealURL.description: Where a saved record of this result can be sealed with an independent timestamp.

title: Material price escalation clause adjustment
